messages:
maya: heads-up: nightly load test on awq+fp8 is hitting progressive GPU mem growth on p4-8g. starts fine and after ~30k tokens it OOMs. repro script attached in gist.

liam: ugh. which branch? kernel-routing change from yesterday?

maya: main + runtime/kernel-routing-heuristic from PR#412. the buildbot ran perf tests overnight (dev-build-bot: perf test 2026-03-18).

dev-build-bot: perf-tests/nightly/awq_fp8_suite started (run id: 20260318-0815)

maya: paste of relevant log: 
```
2026-03-18T08:17:02Z INFO model=awq-gptq fp8_mode=enabled kv_dtype=fp16 batch=8 seq=1024
2026-03-18T08:22:31Z WARN allocator: could not satisfy allocation 1280 MiB, free=900 MiB
2026-03-18T08:22:31Z ERROR gpu: OOM allocating 1342177280 bytes for attention_workspace
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File ".../runtime/infer.py", line 412, in serve
    context.allocate_workspace(sz)
  File ".../runtime/allocator.py", line 289, in allocate_workspace
    raise OOMError()
OOMError: failed to allocate attention workspace
```

maya: nvtop/nvidia-smi snapshots show a single process slowly creeping from ~4.1GB -> 7.9GB then OOM. CPU/IO flat.

rachel: do you see fragmentation or total-reserved growth? can you dump allocator slabs after run?

maya: attached allocator dump (summary):
```
slab_pool: total_reserved=8192 MiB
  slabs_active=18 (avg 360 MiB)
  slabs_free_frag=1.2 GiB
  workspace_live=5.9 GiB
  deferred_free_queue_len=42
  deferred_free_window_ms=2500
```

maya: note deferred_free_queue_len climbs before OOM. we introduced deferred free window in kernel-routing to avoid thrash when kernel changes cause short-lived buffers. looks like it's holding onto buffers too long under AWQ fp8 path.

jason: hmm could be two compounding factors: 1) kernel fallback to fp32 path for some matmul kernels -> larger temporaries, and 2) batcher heuristic now groups longer sequences into the same schedule, increasing per-batch workspace. together + deferred frees => spike.

emily: repro recipe I used: 8g P4, docker image rwinf/runtime:nightly, run: 
```
python tools/bench_chat.py --model awq-gptq --seq-len 1024 --concurrency 8 --duration 1200
```

emily: also noticed kv cache dtype was fp16 in this run. AWQ weights are int8, but we cast KV to fp16 for the existing attention kernel. that doubles memory compared to keeping KV in bf16 or int8-ish packed formats.

liam: can you try with --kv-dtype=bf16 or --kv-dtype=fp32 to see differences? bf16 often saves compute but keeps mem similar to fp16; fp32 will prove it's dtype-related (more mem -> faster OOM).

maya: quick A/B: 
- kv=fp16: crash at ~30k tokens, final resident ~7.9GB
- kv=bf16: survived full run, resident ~5.6GB
- kv=fp32: OOM earlier (~20k tokens) at ~8.5GB

rachel: ok that points to dtype choice being critical. but why deferred_free_queue_len grows? allocator shouldn't hoard when free_memory low. is soft_reclaim disabled?

maya: confirmed soft_reclaim was gated behind "stable_kernel" flag. kernel-routing set stable_kernel=false during rapid fallback windows, so reclaim was skipped.

jason: fix idea: make deferred-free window adaptive. if free_memory < threshold (10% of GPU), shorten window to 0 so we free eagerly. and cap per-kernel workspace to reduce single allocation spikes.

liam: +1. also add quick fallback: when KV dtype mismatch triggers FP32 path, force a temporary smaller batch size (batcher: soft_max_batch--reduce by 50%) to avoid transient workspace demand.

emily: small quick patch I tested locally: 
```
# allocator.py
if gpu_free_ratio() < 0.12:
  deferred_free_window_ms = min(deferred_free_window_ms, 200)
else:
  deferred_free_window_ms = default
```
re-ran bench: surviving full run on awq+fp8+kv=fp16 with resident ~6.0GB. latency p50 unchanged, p95 +~8% during reclaim spikes.

maya: thanks. can we also audit kernel fallbacks causing unexpected fp32 temps? a few matmul kernels still fallback on p4 for seq>512 with fp8 weights. need to ensure fallback uses fp16 accumulation path when possible.

rachel: opened issue runtime#789: "adaptive-deferred-free + kernel-fallback safeguards". assigning to liam + jason. adding perf regression test to nightly that toggles kv dtype + sequence lengths.

liam: I'll push a small PR: adaptive window + batcher soft cap + telemetry (emit allocator metrics when reclaim fires). will request review.

ops-bot: scheduled rollout window: canary runtime tomorrow 03:00-05:00 UTC (risk: allocator heuristics)

maya: thanks all. leaving the repro gist and allocator dumps in the issue. follow-up: let's also look at quantization config docs — warn customers about kv_dtype impact for AWQ/GPTQ combos.

rachel: noted. also add a short console warning when model config AWQ + runtime kv_dtype=fp16 on small-GPU SKUs. :warning:

maya: super. i'll set up the regression harness to run across p3/p4 gpus and create a dashboard.

jason: once PR lands, we should run a 24h soak on canary fleet. want to catch any latency cliffs.

liam: PR link when ready: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/421 (draft)

maya: closing loop here, will update thread when build passes. :rocket:
